title: The evening handoff
subtitle: Couples session · 2 participants
problem: We keep having the same fight about work and phones. Michael says Lucy takes over; Lucy says Michael disappears after work.
sharedNeed: Rest, recognition, and a teammate who assumes good intent.
agreement: When either of you is flooded: say “pause” and name a return time.
The first ten minutes after Michael gets home are device-free.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: Thank you both for making this time. I’m Kinora. I’m here to understand the loop you’re stuck in, not to decide who’s right. Michael, what happened last night?

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: I walked in after a ten-hour day, and before I even put my bag down, Lucy was already on me about my phone. I hadn’t even sat down.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: I’m listening for the moment, not the verdict. Lucy, what did that look like from your side?

lines.speaker: lucy
lines.text: I’d been with the kids since six. He walks in, sits down, starts scrolling, like the house isn’t on fire. I don’t need a helper. I need a partner.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: Two experiences can both be true. Underneath the frustration, Michael, what were you protecting?

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: My one quiet minute. Work has been brutal. If I stop moving, it all catches up with me. And when she comes at me like that, I shut down.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: Lucy, when Michael shuts down, what do you wish he understood?

lines.speaker: lucy
lines.text: That I disappear too. I’m holding all of it, and when he goes quiet, I’m suddenly alone with it. I get loud because quiet doesn’t get me heard.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: What did each of you need in that moment that you didn’t get? Lucy, start with the need under the anger.

lines.speaker: lucy
lines.text: To be seen. Not fixed, seen. And to know I’m not doing this by myself.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: Michael, when Lucy says she doesn’t want to do this by herself, what happens inside you?

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: I feel like I’m failing. No matter how hard I work, I’m still the one letting her down. I need her to know I’m not checked out. I’m just running on empty.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: I hear a shared need: rest, recognition, and a teammate who assumes good intent. You’re both asking for the same thing in different languages. Does that feel fair to each of you?

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: Yeah. I didn’t see it like that.

lines.speaker: lucy
lines.text: Me neither. I thought he just didn’t care.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: So here’s one small agreement. When either of you is flooded, you say pause and name a return time. And the first ten minutes after Michael gets home are device-free. Does that feel doable?

lines.speaker: lucy
lines.text: Ten minutes I can do. But I need him to actually put the phone down.

lines.speaker: michael
lines.text: I can do that. And Lucy... I’m sorry. I didn’t realize the quiet was landing as disappearing.

lines.speaker: lucy
lines.text: I’m sorry too. For coming in hot before you even sat down. I’ll try the pause thing.

lines.speaker: kinora
lines.text: That’s a real agreement, not a resolution of everything. I’ll save it to your summary with one next step: this week, try the five-minute course, Repair After the Storm, together. Thank you both. This was a conversation, not a verdict.
